summary: The patch moves mori-core's two Midnight SDK crates from unconditional [dev-dependencies] to optional [dependencies] gated behind a new non-default feature `midnight-compat-tests`, and places the single Midnight-native compatibility test behind `#[cfg(feature = "midnight-compat-tests")]`, while adding an explicit manual-workflow step and documented command to retain full compatibility coverage. Within the source-only scope, the feature gating preserves the security controls: the three security-critical tests (valid-signature + domain binding, tampering/expiry/malformed-signature rejection, canonical-encoding invariance) remain ungated and run under default features, so the core verify_intent enforcement is still exercised by default; only the external SDK byte-compatibility cross-check is made opt-in. The change uses correct Rust/Cargo idioms (dep: requires optional regular deps; the gated `use` sits inside the gated fn; feature name is consistent across Cargo.toml, #[cfg], and --features; `--test intents` matches tests/intents.rs), keeps the default build SDK-free (no other workspace crate enables the feature, resolver 3 does not unify features into unselected packages), and leaves the compatibility test function byte-identical aside from the one cfg line. No blocking source-integration defect found; I approve source integration. This is a source-only judgment with no runtime/execution admission.
findings: Controls preserved: the security-critical tests in crates/mori-core/tests/intents.rs (genuine_signature_and_bound_domain, tampering_expiry_and_noncanonical_encoding_reject, json_order_does_not_change_signing_bytes) remain ungated and run under default features; only the Midnight-SDK byte-compatibility cross-check (signing_frame_matches_pinned_midnight_native_verifier) is made opt-in behind the non-default feature. This is the correct split and does not weaken the core verify_intent enforcement in the default suite.

SDK-free default achieved and correct: Midnight deps are now optional [dependencies] behind a non-default feature; no src/ code references them, so the default lib/test build pulls no Midnight SDK. This matches the RUST_GUIDELINES mandate (lines 276-277) to keep Midnight deps behind a feature. With resolver=3 and no other workspace crate enabling the feature, `cargo test --workspace --locked` stays SDK-free.

Correct Cargo/cfg idiom: moving the two crates out of [dev-dependencies] is required because `dep:` feature syntax only applies to optional regular dependencies; the gated `use midnight_serialize::Deserializable;` sits inside the cfg-gated function so the feature-off build has no unused-import/missing-dependency error; the feature name `midnight-compat-tests` is consistent across Cargo.toml definition, #[cfg(feature = ...)], and the workflow --features flag; workflow `--test intents` correctly targets tests/intents.rs.

Compat function byte-identical: the only change to tests/intents.rs is the single added `#[cfg(feature = "midnight-compat-tests")]` attribute line above #[test]; the function body is unchanged (verified against the diff context), supporting the byte-identical claim.

Optional compat coverage retained but with reduced automatic enforcement: the gated test is no longer selected by the default `cargo test --workspace --locked`; coverage now depends on the explicitly added manual-workflow step (workflow_dispatch) and the documented `cargo test --features midnight-compat-tests` command. This is consistent with the documented zero-native/manual-CI boundary but shifts the SDK-compatibility regression check from automatic to manual invocation -- recorded as a non-blocking observation.

Minor documentation note (non-blocking, out of changed-source scope): RUST_GUIDELINES.md references `--test continuations` as an SDK-free selection example; that test file is not among the provided inputs so its existence cannot be confirmed here. It is illustrative documentation, not part of the feature's source integration.
